title: The Lab Constellation — every Lab page as a star chart
description: The 100th page: every page in the Lab drawn as a star, with each category forming its own constellation, joined in the order the pages were made and made brighter the more Playwright tests it has. Hover or tap a star for its title, description and thumbnail, click to visit it, filter by category, search titles, tags and descriptions, or take a guided tour that flies through all of them in order.
prompt: For the 100th page, make an interactive map of ALL the Lab pages as a star chart. It can load the site's own data file (../data/projects.js, which defines window.PROJECTS). Place each Lab page as a star clustered by category, so each category is a constellation. Set star brightness by test count and draw lines connecting pages in the same category in id order. Hover or tap should show the title, description and thumbnail, and click should open the page. Add a category filter, search, a tour mode that flies through all 100 in order, and counts per category. It must also work gracefully, with a message and no errors, if PROJECTS is missing.

methodology: The data file is the oracle: every test reads window.PROJECTS itself and derives the expected star list, per-category counts, total tests and search results. The page never checks itself, and the spec keeps working as pages are added.
Layout invariants rather than coordinates: one star per Lab page, stars with more tests are always larger, and every star sits nearer its own constellation's centroid than any other's.

Interaction on both input types: on desktop, hovering shows the card and a click navigates. On touch, the first tap shows the card and the second opens the page; the spec caught a bug where focus-on-tap skipped straight to navigation.
Tour timing under page.clock: it starts at the lowest id, advances once per step, holds while paused, steps with the buttons and arrow keys, wraps at the ends, and closes on Escape.
Graceful failure: page.route() replaces the data file with nothing and then with malformed entries. The page shows an explanatory message, hides the controls and throws no page errors.
risks: The data file is generated by the build; if it lags behind the pages on disk, the chart shows the last build, which is correct behaviour but can surprise.
A missing thumbnail for a brand-new page logs a 404 when hovered, so the image hides itself on error.
Overlap between the info card and the star it describes on small screens; the card moves to the top when the star is in the lower half.
Categories added in future need a colour and a slot; unknown categories fall back to spare colours and extra positions.
qa.playwright: Because the page renders whatever the data file says, the spec treats that file as ground truth and computes every expectation from it with page.evaluate. Tests stay valid at 80 pages today and at 100 after the next build. Stars are real SVG <a> elements with aria-labels, so getByTestId, hover, click and tap all work on them directly. The first mobile run exposed an info card covering the tapped star, found through Playwright's 'element intercepts pointer events' actionability error, which led to a real layout fix. page.route() simulates a missing or corrupt data file without touching the server, and page.clock drives the tour's timers.
coverage: Star count, category counts and total tests match the data; brightness order; cluster separation
Hover card (desktop), tap-then-tap (mobile), thumbnail, links, navigation
Category filter, search with status text, Enter to first match, no-match
Tour start, auto-advance, zoom, pause, next/prev, arrow keys, wrap, Escape
Missing and malformed data file handled without errors

a11y: Every star is a real link with an accessible name (id, title, category, test count), so the sky can be tabbed through, and focusing a star shows its card. Filters are toggle buttons with counts, search results are announced in a live status, and the tour has labelled buttons plus arrow and Escape keys. A 'browse as a list' section gives the same pages as plain grouped links.
